scenes.tts: Every clue so far favoured separate cells. None reached the membrane. What would it take?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Gap, Seen. The three icons from chapter one, each stopping short of the contact.
scenes.narration: Every clue so far favoured separate cells. None reached the membrane. What would it take?

scenes.tts: Suppose you could see the membrane at a contact. What would you see if Golgi were right? And if Kahal were right?
scenes.caption: Suppose you could see the membrane at a contact. What would you see if Golgi were right? And if Cajal were right?
scenes.visual: Predict card: If Golgi were right, what would the electron microscope show here? And if Cajal were right?
scenes.narration: Suppose you could see the membrane at a contact. What would you see if Golgi were right? And if Cajal were right?

scenes.tts: If the branches are fused, the outer membrane runs on around both, and no membrane crosses the junction.
scenes.visual: Sketch one: two processes joined by an open cytoplasmic bridge, the outer plasma membrane enclosing both. No membrane partition across the bridge. Label: continuous cytoplasm; no membrane across the junction.
scenes.narration: If the branches are fused, the outer membrane runs on around both, and no membrane crosses the junction.

scenes.tts: If the cells are separate, two membranes face each other across a gap. Each cytoplasm stops at its own membrane.
scenes.visual: Sketch two: two membrane lines face each other across a gap; each cytoplasm stops at its own membrane.
scenes.narration: If the cells are separate, two membranes face each other across a gap. Each cytoplasm stops at its own membrane.

scenes.tts: The electron microscope could show it, in thin sections of nervous tissue.
scenes.visual: A beam of electrons passes through an ultrathin section. Label: transmission electron microscope.
scenes.narration: The electron microscope could show it, in thin sections of nervous tissue.

scenes.tts: In nineteen fifty-five, De Robertis and Bennett examined synapses in frog and earthworm.
scenes.caption: In 1955, De Robertis and Bennett examined synapses in frog and earthworm.
scenes.visual: On screen: 1955, De Robertis and Bennett. Frog sympathetic ganglia; earthworm nerve cord.
scenes.narration: In 1955, De Robertis and Bennett examined synapses in frog and earthworm.

scenes.tts: In nineteen fifty-six, Sanford Palay examined the rat brain.
scenes.caption: In 1956, Sanford Palay examined the rat brain.
scenes.visual: On screen: 1956, Palay. Rat brain.
scenes.narration: In 1956, Sanford Palay examined the rat brain.

scenes.tts: At the chemical synapses they examined, they saw the second sketch. Two membranes stayed separate across a cleft ten to twenty nanometers wide.
scenes.caption: At the chemical synapses they examined, they saw the second sketch. Two membranes stayed separate across a cleft 10 to 20 nanometres wide.
scenes.visual: Labelled schematic of an electron micrograph builds up: first membrane, second membrane, then the cleft. On screen: cleft 10 to 20 nm in the first reports; about 20 nm usually quoted.
scenes.narration: At the chemical synapses they examined, they saw the second sketch. Two membranes stayed separate across a cleft 10 to 20 nanometres wide.

scenes.tts: Small vesicles crowded the terminal. In such images, the receiving membrane also looks thickened.
scenes.visual: Vesicles fill the presynaptic terminal; a dark thickening lines the postsynaptic membrane. Labels: vesicles, cleft, thickened membrane.
scenes.narration: Small vesicles crowded the terminal. In such images, the receiving membrane also looks thickened.

scenes.tts: Under light, that whole cleft sits inside one blur. The electron microscope replaced the blur with two membranes.
scenes.visual: The chapter one blur disk returns over the schematic, the cleft a sliver inside it, then clears to two sharp membranes. On screen: blur about 200 nm; cleft about 20 nm.
scenes.narration: Under light, that whole cleft sits inside one blur. The electron microscope replaced the blur with two membranes.

scenes.tts: The question was settled, about eighty years after the black reaction.
scenes.visual: Timeline: 1873 black reaction, 1906 Nobel, 1955 and 1956 electron microscopy.
scenes.narration: The question was settled, about eighty years after the black reaction.

scenes.tts: Some neurons are joined more closely. At an electrical synapse, channels called gap junctions cross both membranes.
scenes.visual: Two membranes a few nanometres apart; two rings of six connexins, one in each membrane, dock end to end. Label: gap junction; a few nm.
scenes.narration: Some neurons are joined more closely. At an electrical synapse, channels called gap junctions cross both membranes.

scenes.tts: Ions and small molecules pass straight from one cell into the next.
scenes.visual: Small dots flow through the docked channel from one cell into the other.
scenes.narration: Ions and small molecules pass straight from one cell into the next.

scenes.tts: Does this bring back Golgi's network? What would you inject into one cell to find out?
scenes.visual: Predict card: Does a pore bring back the network? What would you inject?
scenes.narration: Does this bring back Golgi's network? What would you inject into one cell to find out?

scenes.tts: A small tracer such as neuro-biotin passes through to coupled neighbours.
scenes.visual: One cell is injected; a small tracer spreads into two coupled neighbours. On screen: small tracer, such as Neurobiotin.
scenes.narration: A small tracer such as Neurobiotin passes through to coupled neighbours.
scenes.caption: A small tracer such as Neurobiotin passes through to coupled neighbours.

scenes.tts: A ten kilodalton dextran, nearly five nanometers across, stays in the injected cell.
scenes.caption: A 10-kilodalton dextran, nearly 5 nanometres across, stays in the injected cell.
scenes.visual: Large dextran fills only the injected cell, stopped at its membrane. On screen: 10 kDa dextran, nearly 5 nm; vertebrate connexin pore about 1.5 nm.
scenes.narration: A 10-kilodalton dextran, nearly 5 nanometres across, stays in the injected cell.

scenes.tts: In one shared cytoplasm, the dextran would spread too, given time. The electron microscope then confirms two membranes.
scenes.visual: Side panel: a syncytium, one cytoplasm with many nuclei, with the large dye spreading through all of it over time. Then a small inset: an electron micrograph schematic of two membranes at the contact.
scenes.narration: In one shared cytoplasm, the dextran would spread too, given time. The electron microscope then confirms two membranes.

scenes.tts: In vertebrates, Golgi's network does not exist. Coupling through pores that can close does.
scenes.visual: On screen: coupling through regulated pores, not one fused net.
scenes.narration: In vertebrates, Golgi's network does not exist. Coupling through pores that can close does.

scenes.tts: There are exceptions outside vertebrates. The squid giant axon forms from fused fibres. A comb jelly's nerve net shares one membrane.
scenes.visual: Two small insets: a squid giant axon formed from fused fibres of many cells, and a comb jelly's nerve net with one continuous membrane. Label: exceptions, where neurons do fuse.
scenes.narration: There are exceptions outside vertebrates. The squid giant axon forms from fused fibres. A comb jelly's nerve net shares one membrane.

scenes.tts: A touch is not a fusion, and neither is a pore. Separate cells, joined at specialized contacts, are what development has to wire.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: A touch is not a fusion, and neither is a pore. Separate cells joined at specialized contacts are what development wires.
scenes.narration: A touch is not a fusion, and neither is a pore. Separate cells, joined at specialized contacts, are what development has to wire.
